page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance exhibits strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core performance, text processing, and static web serving throughput align with average mid-tier expectations. However, memory subsystem constraints are present; while cached small-block reads perform adequately, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into the weak and poor categories, respectively.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c3d-highcpu-8 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or high-speed local storage. It is well-suited for tasks such as web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate-scale multi-threaded applications. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference due to its constrained memory capacity and lower uncached memory write speeds.
